items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash — one day on, 'full public launch' is contested: most third-party technical references still list it as preview-only (MiniMax Code / Token Plan), Hugging Face returns 401 for M3.1 variants, open-weight date Oct 23 remains vendor-adjacent and unverified, but a second independent anchor (ModelDial 75/57 at max reasoning) now sits alongside Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index 42
items.summary: A day after MarkTechPost framed MiniMax's October 19 announcement as a full public launch, the picture is messier than that single headline suggests, and the enrichment pass is mostly about pinning down what has actually shipped. Four technical references that spent the most time with the model — eesel.ai (across six languages), CometAPI's spec page, Gradually.ai's model card, and OrcaRouter's leak writeup — all still describe M3.1 Flash as preview-only: the model ID is MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview, access is through MiniMax Agent / MiniMax Code and the Token Plan rather than standard pay-as-you-go, reasoning cannot be turned off, and the third-party pricing numbers (BenchLM's $0.15/M input and $0.60/M output; BigGo's '70% cheaper per agent task') do not yet appear on a MiniMax-hosted pricing page any of these sources can cite. On Hugging Face, OrcaRouter reports the MiniMaxAI organization returns 401 for MiniMax-M3.1 and its preview variants, with the most recent public uploads still being MiniMax-Music3 and MiniMax-H3; a 250 GB checkpoint named MiniMax-M3.1-preview-private is referenced in the leak writeup but is not a confirmed public release. The Pasquale Pillitteri claim that open weights land on October 23 therefore remains vendor-adjacent reporting rather than a confirmed MiniMax announcement. The one new independent signal in the overnight window is from ModelDial, a third-party evaluator using private tasks: it scored M3.1-Flash-Preview 75/100 on backend and 57/100 on frontend at maximum reasoning effort, with the explicit note that these scores describe those tasks only — a second independent anchor alongside Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index of 42, not a public standardized benchmark. The vendor-reported benchmark table from launch day remains unchanged: Automation-Bench 62.2 (vs DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 60.5), BankerToolBench 76.2 (ties Claude Opus 5), OSWorld V2 61.7, Agents' Last Exam 29.6, DeepSWE v1.1 73.7, Terminal-Bench 4.0 38.1 (vs Opus 5's 51.8), BabyVision 91%, with CellCog's 62.2-vs-62.8 Automation-Bench discrepancy still unexplained. For comparison, Reflection AI Beam's own Oct 8 revised table — covered in yesterday's am — places its Terminal-Bench v2.1 at 80.1 behind every current open-weight coding leader; MiniMax's Terminal-Bench 4.0 is a different benchmark version, so direct cross-reads are not clean. No Simon Willison coverage or Hacker News front-page thread for M3.1 Flash surfaced from Oct 19 or overnight. Late-breaking pass: Mistral Large 4 weights still due around Oct 27 under custom license, no overnight update; GitHub Universe Oct 28–29 is still pre-event; Reflection AI Beam has no new overnight hook; no credible Tier-1 lab announcement from the Oct 19–20 overnight 12-hour window.
items.why_it_matters: The practical read from launch day stands — if the price point and the agent-benchmark positioning hold up, M3.1 Flash is cheap enough to just try on three or four real tasks and measure, not something to plan around. The overnight pass sharpens the caveats around that read rather than overturning it, and the two things worth sitting with are both about pinning down what has actually shipped. First, 'full public launch' is the MarkTechPost framing; it is not what the technical references are describing. Four separate third-party model pages (eesel.ai, CometAPI, Gradually.ai, OrcaRouter) still use the ID MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview and describe access as going through MiniMax Code and the Token Plan rather than standard pay-as-you-go. The $0.15/M input and $0.60/M output figures that make the whole cheap-and-measure argument work are from BenchLM and MarkTechPost — they do not yet appear on a MiniMax-hosted pricing page that any of these references can point at. For a hobbyist Python workflow, this matters: pulling an API key likely means going through MiniMax Agent / MiniMax Code rather than a generic MiniMax pay-as-you-go endpoint, and the real per-token cost may need confirming at usage time rather than taken as settled. Second, the open-weight story has not moved. Pasquale Pillitteri's Oct 23 release date was already flagged yesterday as unconfirmed by MiniMax directly, and nothing on MiniMax's own channels or Hugging Face organization has changed overnight. OrcaRouter's note that MiniMaxAI returns 401 for MiniMax-M3.1 is the specific technical signal here — the only M3.1-named thing circulating is a leaked 250 GB checkpoint, which is not a release. For Gabe's purposes, assume there is no open-weight M3.1 to download yet, and treat the Oct 23 date as a lead to re-verify, not a plan to act on. The one genuinely new piece of substance is a second independent benchmark anchor: ModelDial scored M3.1-Flash-Preview 75/100 on backend and 57/100 on frontend tasks at maximum reasoning effort. These are private tasks, not a standardized public benchmark, but ModelDial sits in the same category as Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index of 42 — a third-party read that is not identical to the vendor table. The two anchors together paint a consistent picture: competitive at this price tier for backend and tool-using work, materially weaker on frontend/UI-shaped work and on shell-prompt coding (Terminal-Bench 4.0 38.1). The practical path from yesterday still holds. If Gabe wants to measure, pull a key from MiniMax Code or whichever third-party API route is actually live for his region, run three of his real HTML/CSS/Python tasks, and compare output against Sonnet 5.5 (the known-steady baseline) and the Chinese open-weight coding leader sitting highest on OpenRouter this week. The ModelDial result is a mild caution against expecting much on frontend-shaped work; the shell-coding gap is still the one Beam's own Terminal-Bench v2.1 landscape also warned about yesterday.
items.why_it_matters_brief: 'Full public launch' is really MiniMax-Code-only preview access with vendor-adjacent pricing — ModelDial adds a second independent anchor (75/57 backend/frontend at max reasoning), but Oct 23 open-weight date is still unverified.

Third-party API pricing: $0.15/M input, $0.60/M output (BenchLM, MarkTechPost); BigGo frames as ~70% cheaper per agent task. Open weights reportedly due Oct 23 per Pasquale Pillitteri — unconfirmed by MiniMax directly. Space Bunny stealth model confirmed as earlier build of this same model (Unite.ai, BigGo). Both are the cheap-and-measure story this week. takes.source: MarkTechPost — MiniMax Just Launched M3.1 Flash: 428B MoE Agentic Model at $0.15/M Input
takes.take: Primary same-day source. Headlines the $0.15/M input price, 428B MoE architecture with ~23B active, and prints MiniMax's vendor benchmark table (Automation-Bench 62.2 against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 60.5; DeepSWE v1.1 73.7 against DeepSeek V4.1 Flash-1017 77.0; Terminal-Bench 4.0 38.1 against Opus 5 51.8). Flags that open weights are due later in October.

takes.source: Unite.ai — MiniMax Launches M3.1 Flash, Revealing Space Bunny Stealth Model
takes.take: Confirms the Space Bunny stealth-build reveal and the Oct 19 full launch frame. Lists OSWorld V2 61.7, Agents' Last Exam 29.6 and BabyVision 91%, and notes MiniMax's claim of first-place among Chinese models on OSWorld V2 and Agents' Last Exam.

takes.source: BigGo Finance — The mysterious Space Bunny reveals itself
takes.take: The '70% cheaper per agent task' framing comes from here; also prints BankerToolBench 76.2 tying Claude Opus 5. The 70% figure is BigGo's own framing of the pricing delta, not a MiniMax-cited number — treat as a derived figure.

Independent anchor. Scores the model at 42 on the Intelligence Index — well above the ~13 median for its price tier. Describes it as token-efficient for its intelligence level. A formal published breakout analysis has not landed yet.

takes.source: Pasquale Pillitteri — MiniMax announces M3.1 Flash is coming after September preview
takes.take: Dates the preview-to-launch transition and reports the open-weights release as scheduled for October 23. The open-weight timeline is not confirmed by MiniMax directly in sources I could reach from this run or the overnight enrichment pass — treat as a lead to re-verify tomorrow.

takes.source: CellCog — MiniMax M3.1 Flash: Price, Benchmarks, Space Bunny
takes.take: The caution. Flags that Automation-Bench appears as 62.2 in MiniMax's main benchmark table but 62.8 in its maximum-effort cost chart, and notes an 'AutomationBench-AA' variant with a different score. Treat vendor benchmark numbers as a launch pitch, not an audited scoreboard.

Independent hands-on. Reports KingBench 3 coding at 66.25% — a sharp jump from M3's 31.25%, but still behind the top-tier models. The write-up supports the 'competitive at this price tier, not frontier-class on coding' framing.

takes.source: GPTunneL — MiniMax releases M3.1 Flash: agent tasks 70% cheaper
takes.take: Secondary coverage echoing the 70%-cheaper agent-task framing. Useful as corroboration that multiple outlets are using the same cost delta — but the figure traces back to BigGo's derivation, not an independent cost study.

takes.source: eesel.ai — MiniMax M3.1 Flash: specs, pricing, and how to try the preview
takes.take: The access-status read. Documents the model ID as MiniMax-M3.1-Flash-Preview and describes availability as limited to MiniMax Agent / MiniMax Code and the Token Plan, with no standalone pay-as-you-go listing and no Hugging Face model card at the time of writing. The 1M-token context window and five-level reasoning-effort control are confirmed; reasoning cannot be fully turned off. Multiple language variants of this writeup (de, es, fr, pt, nl) all describe the same preview-only access model — treat the headline 'full public launch' framing with caution.

takes.source: Gradually.ai — MiniMax M3.1 Flash Preview model card
takes.take: Introduces a second independent benchmark anchor. ModelDial, a third-party evaluator using private tasks, scored M3.1-Flash-Preview 75/100 on backend and 57/100 on frontend at maximum reasoning effort. ModelDial explicitly notes 'these scores describe those tasks only' — not a standardized public benchmark, but a useful cross-check against the vendor table and Artificial Analysis's Intelligence Index of 42. Lists access through MiniMax Agent Tools and APIs with reasoning that cannot be switched off.

The Hugging Face status read. Reports MiniMaxAI organization returns 401 for MiniMax-M3.1 and preview variants; most recent public uploads are MiniMax-Music3 and MiniMax-H3. References a 250 GB checkpoint named MiniMax-M3.1-preview-private — leak-based, not a confirmed public release. Taken together with Pasquale Pillitteri's unconfirmed Oct 23 date, the practical read is: no M3.1 open weights to download yet, Oct 23 remains a lead to re-verify, not a plan to act on.
